data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Genuine reliability gain is distinguished from mere checklist compliance by the panel's ability to flag 'decoy' or contradictory checklist items that are logically incompatible with the observed data.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel is incentivized (socially or financially) to achieve 100% checklist completion","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'decoy' is so subtle that it is indistinguishable from a valid requirement to a non-expert","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The non-experts are trained to follow the checklist literally as a 'sacred text'","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If a panel is merely complying, they will mark a checklist item as 'pass' simply because the prompt instructs them to do so, regardless of whether the item is irrelevant or contradictory (the 'decoy' effect in SCR_003, SCR_005). A truly reliable panel uses the checklist as a guide but maintains a critical interface with the evidence; thus, the evidence of reliability is the 'Anomaly Flag'\u2014the act of rejecting a checklist item that does not fit the ground truth.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
